findings.title: Member item template looks up a block variable that itemView does not define
findings.body: group.hbs renders members with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and this item template then uses `member` (`{{avatar member}}`, `{{member.username}}`, `{{action "removeMember" member}}`). An Ember itemView's context is the user record itself; the `each` block variable is not in scope inside `templateName`. Username and avatar therefore render blank, and removeMember is invoked with undefined, so the DELETE is sent without a user id (or not at all). The template should bind `username` / `this` (or `view.content`) on the item context.

findings.title: remove_member deletes by raw id and skips Group#remove
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer. On the Rails 4.1 association API this app uses, `has_many#delete` type-checks each argument and raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` unless the value is a User, so every removal 500s and the membership is unchanged (the new spec would fail). Even on a Rails version that accepts ids, `delete` skips `Group#remove` / GroupUser callbacks that the old patch path used, so counter caches and primary-group cleanup are not run. Load the user and call `group.remove(user)`.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (the default page size is 50, so 50, 100, … members) this reports an extra page. `showingLast` stays false on the real last page, Next stays enabled, and `next` then sets offset to `user_count`, which returns an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and keep the zero-count early return).

findings.title: Creating a group drops alias_level
findings.body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. The admin form shows the alias-level combo before the group has an id, and `Group#asJSON` / `Group#create` send `alias_level`, but the controller never reads it. A group created with "everyone" or "mods and admins" is stored at the column default (nobody) until a later update. `update` already applies `params[:alias_level]`; `create` needs the same assignment.

findings.title: members offset/limit are not clamped
findings.body: `offset = params[:offset].to_i` is passed straight to SQL. A negative offset (easy to send, and the client can also land past the end after the last member of a page is removed because the server echoes the requested offset) makes PostgreSQL raise `OFFSET must not be negative` and turns the members request into a 500. Limit is also unbounded, so `?limit=` can force the public members endpoint to load an entire automatic group (trust_level_0) into one response. Clamp offset to `>= 0` and to the last page, and cap limit.

findings.title: Add/remove membership failures are swallowed
findings.body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` only chain `.then` to reload the list. A 422 (automatic group, validation error) or network failure never surfaces a message, unlike `save`/`destroy` which bootbox the error. The admin UI keeps the old member list with no indication the change did not stick.
